question: Why do hospital planners treat a hospital as full when only about 85% of its beds are occupied?
answer: Because emergencies arrive unevenly. A 1999 simulation of an English acute hospital found that above about 85% average occupancy, random surges regularly left no bed free; above 90%, shortages became routine. A spare bed is not waste but a buffer. At 95% occupancy, a busy Monday leaves patients waiting on trolleys in corridors.
move: A system run near its limit fails on its ordinary bad days.
reference: Bagust, Place & Posnett, Dynamics of bed use in accommodating emergency admissions: stochastic simulation model, BMJ, 1999
